title: Union-Find (disjoint sets)
summary: Build a class that merges groups in near-constant time, then use it for Kruskal's MST.
hints: Store two vectors: `parent` (initially `parent[i] = i`, meaning every element is its own root) and `sz` (initially all 1). Use `std::iota(parent.begin(), parent.end(), 0)` to fill the first one. Also keep a `comps` counter starting at `n`.

`find(x)`: follow `parent` until `parent[x] == x`. Add path compression by pointing nodes straight at the root on the way back: `return parent[x] = find(parent[x]);`. `unite(a, b)`: find both roots; if equal return false; otherwise attach the smaller tree under the larger, add the sizes, decrement `comps`, return true.

Kruskal: sort the edges by weight (`std::sort` with a lambda comparing `.w`), then go through them in order and keep an edge only when `unite(u, v)` returns true (it joins two different groups). Sum those weights. If you kept fewer than `n - 1` edges the graph is disconnected: return `-1`.
